USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Clinical titration in encephalopathy

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient recovering from hepatic encephalopathy is alert and has two to three soft stools daily on lactulose. An isolated ammonia value remains above the laboratory reference interval. Which approach best avoids harm from over-treatment?

  1. Clinical status and an appropriate soft-stool pattern
  2. Escalation until every stool becomes liquid
  3. Escalation until ammonia is undetectable
  4. Stopping treatment whenever one ammonia value is elevated
  5. Titration to a fixed rise in serum sodium
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Clinical status and an appropriate soft-stool pattern

Treat the patient and precipitating factors rather than escalating solely to normalize ammonia.

Understanding the options

Clinical status and an appropriate soft-stool pattern
Treat the patient and precipitating factors rather than escalating solely to normalize ammonia.
Escalation until every stool becomes liquid
Watery diarrhea risks dehydration and electrolyte loss.
Escalation until ammonia is undetectable
An undetectable ammonia target is neither necessary nor a safe dosing endpoint.
Stopping treatment whenever one ammonia value is elevated
An elevated value does not establish treatment failure by itself.
Titration to a fixed rise in serum sodium
Serum sodium is a safety variable, not the therapeutic response target.
